comment: Task 81 (census-as-gate): per-demo REQUIRED registered script members. result_schema.py
fails a run whose exercisedMembers census is missing any 'required' member, naming it.
Member spelling is 'ClassSuffix.memberName', suffix-matched against the census's fully
qualified script class names; memberName is the Godot-facing name from the export's
Scope: the census records DISPATCHES ACROSS THE JS<->Kotlin BOUNDARY -- exactly the
surface where the Web dispatch-degradation class of bugs lives (the FPS Enemy.damage
break was a missing dispatch arm). A member invoked Kotlin-to-Kotlin (e.g. via
kotlinScriptInstance) never crosses and CANNOT be required here; such members appear as
'todo' rows with the transitive evidence that covers them. 'todo' rows are honesty
markers, never enforced -- a gap must be visible, not silently omitted.
An absent demo or an empty 'required' list passes (ratchet: tighten as drivers grow).
Every list below was confirmed against a measured envelope before being required.

required.reason: The Area3D overlap that starts the scoring chain; the driver pins the player onto the coin (KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-coin suppresses exactly this).
The scene-wired coin_collected handler updating the Coins label; its only emitter is Player.collectCoin, so this transitively proves the Kotlin-side collect ran.

todo.reason: Called Kotlin-to-Kotlin (Coin.onBodyEntered resolves the Player via kotlinScriptInstance), so it never crosses the recorded dispatch boundary; covered transitively by Hud._on_coin_collected above.

required.reason: MobTimer-driven spawning; without it no mob exists and every other squash assertion is vacuous.
The squashed-signal scoring handler; its only emitter is Mob.squash, so this transitively proves the Kotlin-side squash ran (KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-chase suppresses the choreography).
The lose path: a mob reaching the MobDetector kills the player (KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-death suppresses the ground park that allows it).
The scene-wired hit handler that stops the MobTimer and shows Retry -- the lose path's consequence, one signal downstream of Player.die.

todo.reason: Called Kotlin-to-Kotlin (Player resolves the Mob via kotlinScriptInstance), so it never crosses the recorded dispatch boundary; covered transitively by ScoreLabel._on_Mob_squashed above.

required.reason: The member whose silent dispatch death started task 81: Player's shot reaches the enemy proxy's damage(amount: float) and crosses via callDoubles (task 79/80). Enemies were immortal on Web for weeks while every gate stayed green.
Enemy return fire: the RayCast attack tick that makes the firefight two-sided runs on a scene Timer every run (51 dispatches measured).

Ranked gap #4's assertable half: enemy fire -> Player.damage -> health_updated -> HUD. Player.damage itself is Kotlin-to-Kotlin (invisible to the census), but this handler is its only emitter's consequence -- 7 dispatches measured in a run, from the enemies' timed return fire at the driver's fixed stance.
Ranked gap #10's dispatch half: the weapon-swap chain crosses once at startup every run (hydrates the Weapon resource and instantiates the model the driver's weaponModelInstantiated check watches).

todo.reason: On Web the enemy resolves the Player via kotlinScriptInstance and calls damage Kotlin-to-Kotlin, so the census cannot see the member itself; covered transitively by Hud._on_health_updated above.

required.reason: The driver adds 256 bunnies through this member; the demo's population depends on it.
The driver removes a bunny to advance a handle generation for the stale-handle proof.
The driver's teardown entry: frees the bunnies and reports the final counts.
The driver starts (and later restarts) the round through this member -- the demo's whole lifecycle hangs off it.
Mob spawning; without it the mobsSpawnAndFree evidence is vacuous.
Score ticking during the round.
The round's start delay elapsing is what arms the mob and score timers.

todo.reason: Host-variant lifecycle (task 71: mobs never free on Linux Firefox, cell quarantined). The required-member gate has no per-engine quarantine mechanism, so requiring this would re-litigate the quarantine at the schema layer; the driver's mobsSpawnAndFree check carries it where it holds.
Fires only when a mob happens to hit the stationary player -- nondeterministic inside the smoke window. Driving the game-over transition is ranked gap #5 in the task-81 spec.

required.reason: The driver's synthetic pointer press lands on a board tile; every match/collapse/refill assertion begins here.
The tile press reaching Main's board logic -- the match pipeline's entry.

Tile movement completion: Tile's tween-finished subscriptions are Kotlin lambdas, which dispatch through the aggregate callback key (56 measured across a run) -- the evidence that collapse/refill tiles finished moving, not merely started.

todo.reason: Registered, but invoked from trackedTween's Kotlin tween-finished lambda (Tile.kt), so it never crosses as a named member; the movement evidence is the aggregate row above.
Fires when a sound effect ENDS, which races the driver's window; requiring it would gate on timing, not gameplay.

required.reason: Every build/demolish/rotate/save/load action is handled inside Builder's _process input polling -- the demo registers no gameplay methods at all, so this virtual is the only member-level evidence; the driver's GridMap content checks remain the substantive gameplay gate.

todo.reason: Placement sounds end asynchronously; requiring it would gate on timing. The demo's registered-member surface is otherwise empty (2 members total in the census table).

required.reason: The task-80 dispatch-shape conformance probe the driver calls explicitly; if it stops dispatching, the whole conformance family went dark.
The task-82 coroutine frame-scheduler conformance probe the driver calls explicitly.

todo.reason: Walk-over choreography, engine/host-sensitive: 2 dispatches measured on chrome, but the first gated CI run (kanama#168, run 31542371765) measured ZERO on the runner's firefox -- the walk does not reliably reach a coin there (the same slow-rendering-host class as task 87). Re-require once the driver pins onto a coin deterministically, the platformer pattern.

The one gameplay method observed dispatching (2x, chrome) -- the impact-sound contact handler while the driver holds drive input. Promote to required once its determinism is established across engines/hosts; the rest of racing's members stay dark (spec table: 3 of 5 never invoked) pending driver work.

required.reason: The driver's combat entry (method#3): dispatches the desktop smoke's ported damage routines. If this stops crossing, the two damage members below lose their driver.

Task 81 fix #3: the (VECTOR3, VECTOR3) registered-method shape, the FPS damage bug's sibling -- the desktop SmokeQuit tested it, the Web path dispatched it zero times until smoke_combat. Measured on chrome AND firefox envelopes 2026-08-12; KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-combat suppresses exactly this.
The second desktop damage routine (kotlin-src/SmokeQuit.kt:267 sibling), same shape and evidence as BeeBot.damage; the driver additionally asserts both death frees via liveScriptsByClass.

PROMOTED 2026-08-20 (task 64 coin economy). Same (VECTOR3, VECTOR3) shape as the two bot damage members, and the one a BeetleBot attack / bee Bullet lands in play via collider.call. It was a 'todo' for two successive reasons: first it FAULTED on Web (loseCoins -> CoinsContainer's tween_property passes a NUMBER, and the Web backend had no scalar arm -- task 81 confirmed break #3, which is why the driver still runs combat BEFORE movement), then, once task 64 landed the scalar arm (opcode 289), because NO DRIVER SPILLED COINS so the member was never exercised. thirdperson.mjs's coin-economy phase now dispatches it directly. MEASURED on chrome (3 runs) AND firefox 2026-08-20, protocol 21: census Player.damage = 1, crossings.coinsSpilled = 5, callbackErrors 0, teardown still draining to zero handles. KANAMA_WEB_T81_FALSIFY=no-coins suppresses exactly this.

The coin-economy phase seeds the player's purse with five of these before the spill (loseCoins only spawns min(coins, 5) coins, so an empty purse spills nothing). Each one also runs the CoinsContainer scalar tween, so a regressed task-64 arm faults HERE, before the spill, rather than silently skipping it. MEASURED on chrome (3 runs) AND firefox 2026-08-20: census Player.collect_coin = 5.

The vacuum tween's per-step callback, dispatched BY NAME through the engine's Tween (tween_method) -- i.e. a real JS<->Kotlin crossing, not a Kotlin-to-Kotlin call. It is the first gameplay member on Web whose dispatcher is a Tween interpolation rather than a proxy method or a virtual. The dispatch COUNT is host-paced (chrome 20, firefox 145 for the same five coins, because the tween interpolates per rendered frame), so only its presence is required, never a magnitude. MEASURED 2026-08-20.

The vacuum tween's terminal callback (tween_callback), one per collected coin, and the ONLY boundary-crossing evidence that the coin actually reached the player: it is what re-enters Player.collectCoin -> CoinsContainer.updateCoinsAmount -> the scalar tween. Exactly one per coin on both engines, so unlike _follow this one IS counted: MEASURED chrome (3 runs) and firefox 2026-08-20, 5 dispatches for 5 spilled coins, callbackErrors 0.

todo.reason: Same (VECTOR3, VECTOR3) shape, but no driver choreography destroys a box yet (the desktop smoke does not call it either); the grenade/bullet paths that reach it are ranked gaps #8/#9 in the task-81 spec.

The coin HUD's only registered member, and the caller of the NUMBER tween_property that task 64 fixed -- but it CANNOT be required here: Player holds the container through kotlinScriptInstance<CoinsContainer>() and calls it Kotlin-to-Kotlin, so it never crosses the boundary the census watches. Transitive evidence instead: Player.collect_coin and Coin._collect are required above, both of them call it on the very next line, and the run's noCallbackFaults check fails if its tween finds no scalar arm (that is exactly how the pre-task-64 boundary died). Requiring it would need a driver-reachable caller, which the demo does not have.
Reached only from Player.damage, in-Kotlin, so it never crosses. Covered transitively: Player.damage is required above and crossings.coinsSpilled (5) is the count of coins this member instantiated.

Called Kotlin-to-Kotlin by whoever bursts the coins (Player.loseCoins, BeeBot/BeetleBot death). Covered transitively by Coin._follow/_collect: nothing tweens home unless spawn connected the detection area first.
Ranked gap #6 (win AND lose dark): the driver drives movement but neither the flag win nor the kill-plane reset (task 82's cc find). Requires driver choreography first.
Ranked gap #7: the driver moves the player but never lands a shot; RedRobot.hit / Part.explode stay dark until the combat choreography is written.
